Subject: Next step: technical deep-dive (60-90m) — slot options & prep

Hi Sanjay / Leah,

Thanks again for taking the discovery call earlier today — really useful to understand MediaQuest's ingestion patterns and the low-latency requirements on your personalization features. To keep momentum, we'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive with our ML Infra engineer and solutions architect. Goals for the session:

- Walk through production traffic shape and latency SLOs
- Review model candidate list and quantization/precision constraints
- Validate data residency / network constraints for a Private deployment
- Agree on success criteria and next milestones (POC scope)

Please pick any 60–90 minute slot from the options below (all times PDT):
- Tue Jul 21: 09:00–10:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed Jul 22: 11:00–12:30
- Thu Jul 23: 08:30–10:00 or 16:00–17:30

If none of the above work, propose 2 alternatives and we’ll accommodate. For prep, it would be very helpful if you can share:
- Sample batch of anonymized request traces (token lengths, throughput) or a summary table
- Any constraint list for on-prem/VPC IP allowlists
- Primary success metrics (p50/p95 latency targets, cost per 1M tokens threshold)

I’m copying Vivek (SE) who will run the technical portion and Monica (CS) who will help scope the POC and create the mutual action plan.

Thanks — Rishi

Thanks for confirming, Sanjay — putting the invite on calendar for Wed Jul 22, 11:00–12:30 PDT (90m). Quick logistics and agenda below. Calendar invite will follow from our scheduling system.

Agenda (90m):
1) Intros & goals (5m)
2) Traffic profile & performance targets — MediaQuest data walk-through (15m)
3) Redwood serving runtime overview (KV cache, batching, sequence handling) (15m)
4) Model selection & quantization tradeoffs (20m)
5) Network/security constraints & Private deployment checklist (15m)
6) POC scope, timelines, and next steps (15m)

Prep items we’d like before the call (if possible):
- Sample traces or a 1-page summary (shape: tokens per request, avg/max sequence lengths, RPS distribution) — thanks for the CSV
- IP ranges / firewall egress requirements (we received mediaquest_ip_ranges.txt — can you also confirm NAT/GW details?)
- Any redlines for data residency or retention we should factor into the POC
- Primary engineering contact (Leah) and security contact for follow-ups

Security note: Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and we do have HSM-backed KMS as an enterprise option — I’ll have our security engineer on the call to detail what we can offer and what requires enterprise licensing.

Attachments included: RDW_TDX_Agenda_MediaQuest_v1.pdf (agenda & prep checklist), network-ip-list.txt (summary).

Looking forward — Vivek
